items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23
items.q: Now, what I've learned was through Perkins. ... He'd teach me and show me just what to do and where to make my stops

ctx.x: They used to come around, you know. And there was a fellow by the name of Perkins. You might have heard of him. Dave Perkins. Yes. You heard of him? Yes. Well, he was a wonderful. Oh, he was a fine musician. Oh, you couldn't take it away from him. He used to show these kids, come around with me and show these kids how to hold the instruments, and how to blow the instruments, you understand. And I'd be holding the hoistlets right on, right on in my basement.
See? That first band you had with all the flags, was that right after that exposition they had up in Audubon Park?

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] He played, that time he played with him and Pacquet and Dave Perkins. ... [INTERVIEWEE] You heard of Ashil Pacquet playing clarinet, haven't you? He played good, he played good.

ctx.x: He was good. He was good.

Give them all chords and spades and beat them out. Yeah. And Perkins was a trombone player but Perkins couldn't hold a trombone player alongside Humpback Gallaty, Bill Gallaty. Bill Gallaty. Oh, that's the father of the present trumpet player.
Bill Gallaty. He's playing trumpet, his son?

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1964-04-25
items.q: That's the way Perkins learned us how to play. ... he tried to manage to teach them and show them

ctx.x: What about Dave Perkins? Yes, way older than me.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Alfred Laine Interview, 1951-04-21
items.q: the man that I first started with was Dave Perkins

ctx.x: Well, who is the gentleman that taught you how?

Well, the man that I first started with was Dave Perkins. And ever since Dave Perkins, I went with another guy that used to play. His name was Meade, Will Meade. He was an awful good professor. Well, now that's been some years ago. He had a cigar stand on Royal and Espenade. That's where I used to go to. He was a mighty nice musician too.
Jack, how far from this section that we are right now have you lived? Have you always lived in this neck of the woods? Well, Doctor, fortunately I did.
